incidents.title: Heavy haze and particulate smell near the north industrial estate
incidents.description: Visibility dropped to under 200 m this morning. Eyes and throat irritation reported by residents near the estate boundary.

incidents.title: Dust haze near the cement works, borderline reading
incidents.description: Workers at the neighbouring facility reported mild eye irritation since early morning. The reading is close to the daily limit.

incidents.title: Slight haze reported near the freight depot
incidents.description: A resident reported a faint smoky smell in the early morning. Readings appear within normal seasonal variation for this area.

standards.name: CPCB NAAQS
standards.excerpt: The National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) prescribed by CPCB set the 24-hour average concentration standard for PM2.5 at 60 µg/m³ for residential, rural and other areas. Exceedance of this standard indicates that air quality has deteriorated beyond the acceptable threshold for public health protection.

standards.name: CPCB NAAQS
standards.excerpt: The CPCB NAAQS standard for PM10 sets the 24-hour average concentration limit at 100 µg/m³ for residential, rural and other areas. Values above this limit indicate elevated coarse particulate levels that may adversely affect respiratory health.

standards.name: WHO Air Quality Guidelines 2021
standards.excerpt: The WHO Air Quality Guidelines (2021) recommend a 24-hour mean PM2.5 concentration not exceeding 15 µg/m³. This is a health guideline, not an Indian legal standard. Exceedance indicates elevated health risk under global best-practice thresholds.
